Comment: Dependent pronoun clitics (o=, e=, i=) function as absolutive markers cross-referenced on the verb.
1sg: on (independent/ERG) vs. o= (dependent/ABS); ergative alignment on 1st person.
2sg: en (independent/ERG) vs. e= (dependent/ABS); ergative alignment on 2nd person.
3rd person is three-way: independent te for A; dependent i= for P; coreferential te= for S. No clean ERG-ABS split.
Explicitly stated: 'there are no nominative, ergative or absolutive case markers as affixes on nouns' (p.153). Full NPs carry zero case marking.
Imperfective (marked -ra) clauses maintain ERG-ABS alignment with pronominal arguments.
Perfective (unmarked verb) clauses also maintain ERG-ABS alignment.
Past events expressed with unmarked verb form; ERG-ABS alignment maintained.
Future clauses (projective marker kom) maintain ERG alignment.
Indicative clauses maintain ERG-ABS alignment.
Interrogative mood maintains ERG alignment; imperative shifts to NOM-ACC pattern (absolutive-clitic subjects).
Realis clauses are consistently ERG-ABS.
Future tense (irrealis) and interrogatives (irrealis-like) maintain ERG alignment.
Agentive A arguments take independent ergative pronouns (on/en/te); S and P take dependent absolutive clitics.

Experiencer/non-agentive predicates (fear, hear) are INTRANSITIVE in Akuntsu; their single argument takes the absolutive dependent clitic, not the ergative independent pronoun (e=pip 'you are afraid', o=apinom 'I hear'). Corrected from original value of 1.
Topical A (1st/2nd person) take independent ERG pronouns consistently.
Non-topical A in transitive clauses also uses independent pronouns.
Animate pronominal A (humans) take independent ERG pronouns.
Ergativity is limited to pronominal arguments; inanimate A (full NPs) follow neutral alignment.
Main clause transitive constructions consistently show ERG-ABS alignment.
Aragon (2014: 205, fn.114) explicitly states: 'Additional aspects of ergativity, particularly in complex sentences, is still under investigation.'
Split ergativity conditioned by: (1) pronoun vs. full NP status, (2) person hierarchy (1/2 > 3), (3) patient animacy, (4) verbal mood.
Ergative = independent pronouns (on/en/te); genitive = dependent pronouns (o=/e=/i=). Different paradigm sets.
Instrumental = oblique clitic =(b)o (p.154); comitative = postposition ete (pp.156, 159). Both distinct from independent ERG pronouns.
